title: Plugged in, not charging
fullDescription: ASUS ZenBook and ROG laptops often display 'Plugged in, not charging' when the MyASUS or Battery Health Charging is set to limit charge to 60% or 80%, or when the adapter is underspec.

fixSteps.title: Open MyASUS
fixSteps.instruction: Open MyASUS, Customization > Battery Health Charging > set to Full Capacity Mode.

fixSteps.title: Use OEM adapter
fixSteps.instruction: Use the original ASUS adapter rated for your model wattage.

fixSteps.title: Reset battery
fixSteps.instruction: Hold power 40 seconds with battery and AC disconnected (if removable).

videoSearchQuery: ASUS plugged in not charging fix

faq.a: Extends battery lifespan but can confuse users.

title: Blue Screen of Death (Windows)
fullDescription: ASUS laptops often suffer BSODs from Armoury Crate driver conflicts, failing Intel storage drivers, or aggressive ASUS Optimization service updates. Generic causes also apply (RAM, drivers).

fixSteps.title: Check stop code
fixSteps.instruction: Note the stop code shown on BSOD and look up specific cause.

fixSteps.title: Update or remove Armoury Crate
fixSteps.instruction: Use ASUS Uninstall Tool to fully remove and reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Test RAM and drivers
fixSteps.instruction: Run MemTest86 and update chipset/GPU drivers.

title: WHEA uncorrectable error
fullDescription: WHEA on ASUS ROG laptops often results from auto-overclocking via Armoury Crate or aggressive undervolt profile that becomes unstable.

fixSteps.title: Set Performance to Standard
fixSteps.instruction: Open Armoury Crate, set CPU profile to Standard / Silent.

fixSteps.title: Repaste CPU
fixSteps.instruction: Replace thermal paste with high-quality compound or liquid metal (advanced).

whenToCallPro: If thermal repaste needed and unfamiliar.

faq.a: Use only if confident; risky on ASUS.

title: Powers on but no POST
shortDescription: Fans spin but no display, no boot.
fullDescription: ASUS ROG laptops sometimes power on but never POST. Often caused by failed RAM training, BIOS corruption, or failed dGPU on AMD Advantage models.

fixSteps.title: Drain power
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect AC and battery, hold power 60 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Reseat RAM
fixSteps.instruction: Open bottom cover, reseat SO-DIMM modules if user-accessible.

fixSteps.title: BIOS recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Use ASUS CrashFree BIOS recovery via USB (rename BIOS file appropriately).

whenToCallPro: If recovery and reseating don't help.
videoSearchQuery: ASUS ROG no POST black screen fix

title: Keyboard backlight off
shortDescription: RGB or white backlight stopped working.
fullDescription: ASUS keyboard backlight is controlled via Armoury Crate / Aura Sync. After Windows update, the service can fail and backlight stays off.

fixSteps.title: Try Fn+F3 / Fn+F4
fixSteps.instruction: Press Fn+F4 to increase backlight brightness.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall Armoury Crate
fixSteps.instruction: Use ASUS Uninstall tool, then reinstall fresh from MS Store.

videoSearchQuery: ASUS keyboard backlight not working fix

faq.a: ROG models use F3/F4, others vary.

title: Touchpad / NumberPad not working
fullDescription: ASUS ZenBook with NumberPad uses a hardware touchpad with capacitive number overlay. Pressing the icon top-right toggles to numpad. Sometimes the touchpad gets stuck in numpad mode.

fixSteps.title: Hold NumberPad icon
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the calculator icon (top-right of touchpad) for 0.5s to exit numpad.

videoSearchQuery: ASUS ZenBook touchpad not working fix

title: Cooling fan not spinning
fullDescription: ROG laptops use 0-RPM mode where fans stop below certain temperature. Sometimes this gets stuck or one fan fails entirely. Check Armoury Crate fan profile and listen for both fans.
symptoms: Hot under load with no fan

fixSteps.title: Set Turbo profile
fixSteps.instruction: In Armoury Crate set Turbo mode to verify fan spins under load.

fixSteps.title: Stress test
fixSteps.instruction: Run Cinebench or FurMark to confirm both fans engage.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed fan
fixSteps.instruction: Open laptop, replace failed fan with matching part.

videoSearchQuery: ASUS ROG fan not spinning fix

title: Screen flickering
shortDescription: Display flickers, especially on AMD models.
fullDescription: ASUS laptops with AMD Ryzen and high-refresh displays sometimes flicker due to PSR (Panel Self Refresh) issues, driver problems, or eDP cable wear.

fixSteps.title: Disable PSR
fixSteps.instruction: Use AMD Software or Intel Graphics Command Center to disable Panel Self Refresh.

fixSteps.title: Replace eDP cable
fixSteps.instruction: If flicker persists at BIOS too, replace cable.

whenToCallPro: For cable replacement on slim models.

faq.a: Yes if it causes flicker; small battery cost.

title: ZenBook won't turn on
fullDescription: ZenBook laptops sometimes die completely after deep discharge. ASUS provides a hard reset procedure: hold power 40 seconds with AC disconnected.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect AC, hold power 40 seconds, plug AC back in, wait 10 minutes, try power.

fixSteps.title: Try different adapter
fixSteps.instruction: Use a known-good ASUS or 65W+ USB-C PD adapter.

videoSearchQuery: ASUS ZenBook won't turn on fix

faq.a: Forces EC and capacitors to fully discharge.

title: DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE BSOD
shortDescription: Driver did not respond during sleep/wake.
fullDescription: Common BSOD on ASUS laptops when waking from sleep. Caused by Wi-Fi, GPU, or chipset driver not transitioning power states correctly.

fixSteps.title: Update all drivers
fixSteps.instruction: Use MyASUS to update drivers and BIOS.

fixSteps.title: Disable fast startup
fixSteps.instruction: Power options > Choose what power buttons do > uncheck Turn on fast startup.

fixSteps.title: Roll back driver
fixSteps.instruction: If BSOD started after update, roll back the offending driver.

faq.a: Yes, slightly slower boot but more stable.
